title: Anticipatory Degradation and Connection Guardrails for Downstream Resilience
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an anticipatory degradation framework and connection guardrails to improve downstream dependency resilience (Redis/Kafka/DB). Goals: detect early signs of saturation, proactively shed low-value work, and perform targeted connection eviction to preserve token-level SLOs during partial failures and multi-region incidents.
background: We observed multiple incidents where a saturating Redis or remote DB caused systemic tail latency spikes that cascaded into user-facing errors. Existing circuit-breakers trigger too late (timeout-driven) and our connection pools exhaust under fanout, amplifying failures. This ticket designs and implements a proactive, SLO-driven mitigation path that intervenes before hard failures, coordinating across per-tenant priorities and multi-region routing policies.
goals: Reduce 95th percentile token-generation latency amplification during downstream saturation by >30% under synthetic overload
Keep error-rate increase under 2x baseline for high-priority tenants during degraded periods
Provide safe degraded read-mode for non-critical flows (embeddings backfills, background reranks) with explicit fallbacks
Expose observability: per-tenant admission, eviction, and shed-rate metrics in Console and Grafana
approach: Add a predictive health scoring pipeline for downstream pools that combines: short-window p95/p99 latency deltas, error-rate derivatives, and queue-depth signals

Implement a two-stage pool intervention: (1) soft admission control (per-route probabilistic drop based on tenant score), (2) targeted connection eviction using LRU+weighting for long-lived connections to unhealthy shards
Introduce lightweight early-tripping circuit with hysteresis that routes requests to local cached KV or downgraded model variant instead of remote store when score exceeds threshold
Coordinate with smart routing to prefer healthy regions for high-priority tenants and to route shed traffic to low-cost fallbacks
Instrumentation: add shed_trace_id to requests, new Console panel for "Degradation Events" and Grafana dashboards for pool_score, shed_rate, evicted_conn_count
design_decisions: Use probabilistic shedding (client-aware, tenant-weighted) instead of strict hard quotas to preserve some capacity for mid-priority traffic
Evict long-lived client connections before cutting short new ephemeral connections to minimize warm-KV cache loss for hot paths
Hysteresis windows: 30s ramp to trigger, 90s cooldown to clear to avoid oscillation—tuned from spike tests
Fallback order: local prefix-KV cache -> read-only degraded replica -> model-variant-with-smaller-context -> error fallback
Fail-open only for telemetry (do not fail-open for auth/enforcement code paths)
work_items: Spike: implement pool_score telemetry and run chaos tests against Redis clusters (done)

acceptance_criteria: Synthetic overload test: under 3x normal Redis latency, global token-generation p95 increases by no more than 15% (baseline target)
High-priority tenant SLA: error-rate increase <2x baseline in degradation window
Automated chaos test: pool_score triggers eviction and shed events logged in Console; rollback path tested
Integration: admission controller deployed to canary cluster and validated against canary workload
Telemetry: new Grafana panels show meaningful correlates (pool_score, shed_rate, evicted_conn_count) for at least 48h
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-shedding low-value traffic reduces revenue-sensitive usage. Mitigation: tenant-weighted shedding with explicit revenue tags and opt-outs for concierge customers.

Risk: eviction of long-lived connections could blow cold-KV cache and increase load. Mitigation: prefer evicting idle connections > 5m with lowest affinity score and warm-up via background prefetch for hot keys.
Risk: hysteresis misconfiguration causes oscillation. Mitigation: automated tuning job during canary using A/B with different windows and roll back automatedly if oscillation detected.
Risk: complexity across runtime and gateway increases regression surface. Mitigation: incremental rollout, feature flag gating, and preflight integration tests in CI
notes: Spike results: adaptive eviction reduced p95 from 360ms -> 245ms in Redis-slow scenario (test cluster alpha-2)
Found two client libraries that hold connections open for >10m unintentionally; created follow-up ENG-658402 to mitigate
